key_insight: Helix4D adapts the expressive Trellis2 image-to-3D representation to video-conditioned 4D mesh generation, enabling frame-local attention to share information across time while preserving pretrained robustness on rare, challenging cases.
problem_solved: Enables robust dynamic mesh reconstruction from video for scenes with complex topology changes, transparent materials, thin structures, and inner surfaces that break existing video-to-4D methods.
method: Adapt Trellis2's frame-local representation from image-to-3D to a video-conditioned 4D pipeline.
Enable cross-frame information sharing (temporal aggregation / motion-aware attention) while retaining pretrained handling of rare visual phenomena.
Output coherent dynamic meshes that capture topology changes and internal/transparent geometry across time.
impact: Helix4D makes dynamic, high-fidelity 4D mesh generation practical for complex real-world scenes, improving downstream tasks like animation, AR/VR content creation, and simulation where temporal and geometric fidelity matter.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison: video frames → 4D meshes showing improved handling of topology changes and thin/transparent structures.
Schematic diagram: Trellis2 frame-local attention vs. Helix4D temporal cross-frame sharing (flow arrows + attention heatmaps).
Sequence visualization: time-lapse of a dynamic mesh showing preserved inner surfaces and coherent topology across frames.
Icon set: transparency, thin-structure, topology-change, temporal-consistency to quickly convey challenges addressed.
paper_authors: Jiraphon Yenphraphai, Jianqi Chen, Jian Wang, Gordon Qian, Sergey Tulyakov
